sentences.text: Pulmonary embolism -LRB- PE -RRB- is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has traveled from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream -LRB- embolism -RRB- .	artery in the lungs	pulmonary artery	embolism	embolism
Symptoms of a PE may include shortness of breath , chest pain particularly upon breathing in , and coughing up blood .	chest pain	chest pain	shortness of breath	dyspnea
Symptoms of a blood clot in the leg may also be present such as a red , warm , swollen , and painful leg .	blood clot in the leg	deep vein thrombosis	blood clot	blood clot

Signs of a PE include low blood oxygen levels , rapid breathing , rapid heart rate , and sometimes a mild fever .	oxygen levels	oxygen saturation	rapid breathing	tachypnea	rapid heart rate	tachycardia	fever	fever
Severe cases can lead to passing out , abnormally low blood pressure , and sudden death .	abnormally low blood pressure	shock (circulatory)	sudden death	cardiac arrest	passing out	Syncope (medicine)
PE usually results from a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lung .	blood clot in the leg	deep vein thrombosis	blood clot	blood clot

The risk of blood clots is increased by cancer , prolonged bed rest , smoking , stroke , certain genetic conditions , estrogen-based medication , pregnancy , obesity , and after some types of surgery .	bed rest	bed rest	smoking	smoking	stroke	stroke	genetic	genetics	estrogen-based medication	hormone replacement therapy	pregnancy	pregnancy	obesity	obesity	cancer	cancer
A small proportion of cases are due to the embolization of air , fat , or amniotic fluid .	air	air embolism	fat	fat embolism	amniotic fluid	amniotic fluid embolism
Diagnosis is based on signs and symptoms in combination with test results .
If the risk is low a blood test known as a D-dimer will rule out the condition .	D-dimer	D-dimer

Otherwise a CT pulmonary angiography , lung ventilation/perfusion scan , or ultrasound of the legs may confirm the diagnosis .	CT pulmonary angiography	CT pulmonary angiography	lung ventilation/perfusion scan	lung ventilation/perfusion scan	ultrasound	ultrasound
Together deep vein thrombosis and PE are known as venous thromboembolism -LRB- VTE -RRB- .	deep vein thrombosis	deep vein thrombosis	venous thromboembolism	venous thromboembolism

Efforts to prevent PE include beginning to move as soon as possible after surgery , lower leg exercises during periods of sitting , and the use of blood thinners after some types of surgery .	blood thinners	anticoagulant
Treatment is typically with blood thinners such as heparin or warfarin .	heparin	heparin	warfarin	warfarin	blood thinners	anticoagulant
Often these are recommended for six months or longer .

Severe cases may require thrombolysis using medication such as tissue plasminogen activator -LRB- tPA -RRB- , or may require surgery such as a pulmonary thrombectomy .	thrombolysis	thrombolysis	tissue plasminogen activator	tissue plasminogen activator	pulmonary thrombectomy	pulmonary thrombectomy
If blood thinners are not appropriate , a vena cava filter may be used .	blood thinners	anticoagulant	vena cava filter	vena cava filter
Pulmonary emboli affect about 430,000 people each year in Europe .
In the United States between 300,000 and 600,000 cases occur each year , which results in between 50,000 and 200,000 deaths .
Rates are similar in males and females .
They become more common as people get older .
